Last night  I craved Indian food and logged on to Yelp for help. My very favorite place is 18 miles away and I wanted something nearby.  I found Tandoori Times and arrived there at 8PM.  I couldn't believe that at 8PM there were 10 people ahead of us waiting for a table. \"" A good sign \""I thought or \""poor management that can't handle a crowd?\""  Someone who appeared to be the owner was busy working to see that everyone got a table quickly.  We got a table in 10 minutes in a small room they have in the rear of the restaurant.  Within 5 minutes we got a waitress and placed our order.  She brought us condiments (a red spicy sauce, coriander chili sauce and a spicy sauce made with marinated ginger bits.   No papadums.  Most restaurants give you papadums.  We missed them.  My order of Chicken Vindaloo was absolutely delightful spiced just as I requested HOT.  Our double order of bread came hot and delish(we don't eat rice).  My husband's Lamb Tikka was generous and nicely done.  During our meal, the belly dancer started her act.  This meant that the loud music would soon begin.  AND I MEAN LOUD.  I don't know if it was that we were in that small room, but my eardrums were about to burst.  There was no relief until we ended our meal.  The belly dancer could not be seen from our room so we stood up to peek at what was going on.  It was an attractive young lady, dressing in belly dancing garb dancing to Indian pop music.  Not really belly dancing.  (I've done belly dancing myself.)  Next, dessert.  I ordered the Kheer.  It was absolutely amazing.  It was creamy with sliced almonds and raisins.  Probably one of the best I've had anywhere.  \nI gave Tandoori Times 4 stars because the music was too loud and it kind of spoiled the experience for us.  Other than that the food is really authentic and delicious.  I hope that the management will consider toning down the music at least for the poor people in the back room.  I would never accept a seat in that room when I return.  AND, I will return.

I really wanted to like this salon.  It has a cool concept with the art work and the tattoo artists that are there.  It is in a cute spot!  I just did not have the best experience.  I went in to donate my hair for locks of love.  I found this place by a google search for places who are familiar with the donation.  Julie booked my appointment and even changed my time to later because of work! Excellent right?  Yes, so far I was off to a good start.  I had measured my hair length the night before and figured 10 inches would be right at my shoulder blades.  When I sat  down in the chair with Julie we discussed my hair style, I even showed her pictures of a couple styles I liked.  She then informed me that she did not have a tape measure.  Her co-worker offered her a comb that had a ruler. Great we measured what we not agreed on 10 inches.  Her co-worker then says, well cut above the pony tail holder.  I could not see where the pony tail holder was in relation to the measure line.  Julie then started to cut...OMG it was three inches below my ears.  Oh god!  It was not like I could glue my hair back on.  She then proceeded with the color.  Meh.  It was all over dark brown, I had some highlights in the front, she said they might show through but they showed through REALLY bad!  The next day at work under the fluorescent lights it was really pronounced.  So now onto the cut.  I had told Julie that  I had wanted to make sure my hair could go into a pony tai.  She had mentioned an angled bob.  I told her I had that style in the past and did not want it again because it was a pain to grow back out.  Well, like the pony tail cutting process, she went ahead and cut it the way SHE wanted it.  The hair on the very back of my head is about two inches long ;(  I paid her the $70 for the cut and color and even tipped her $20 but I will not be back.  I went home and measured my pony tail and it was 15 inches.  How does 10 inches off turn into 15... that is such a huge difference.  I really wish that I had been listened to when having such a personal thing as having that much hair cut off.  \nLike I said I did really want to like this place but I just did not have that great of experience....

I am from Santa Barbara and had eaten several times at the original one.  Having been disappointed by some of the other hamburger chains that have come in here in the last few years with much fanfare from people that came from the same towns I was worried that a hamburger from my own home town might be a let down from either a taste or value stand point.  I need not have worried.  I took a friend with me and we each had a mushroom swiss  burger and I had onion rings and she had sweet potato fries.  We both liked the food.  2 burgers, 2 drinks, fries and onion rings were under $19 incl tax.  And being a lovely day we found a spot on the patio and camped out for over an hour.  The staff was friendly and close to being too attentive.  Parking sucks.  Even after the original opening hype they are still packed for a Sunday lunch so they must be doing something right.  I know I will return.
